title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 82-84): Grothendieck sets up a general lemma for presenting a groupoid that sits over another groupoid. The data are a morphism of groupoids p: T~ -> T, a family of arrows (ũ_i)_{i in I} in T~, and its image (u_i) in T, which is assumed to generate T.

Presentation of T. T is presented on the generators u_i as follows:
- Introduce signed indices I' = I x {±1}, with u'_{(i,ε)} = u_i^ε.
- A relation is a word i'_α = (i'_{α,1}, ..., i'_{α,n_α}) in I'^{n_α}, one for each α in A.
- The corresponding arrows u'_{i'_{α,1}}, ..., u'_{i'_{α,n_α}} are assumed composable and to form a loop (lacet).
- The relation (8) reads M_α((u_i)) := u'_{i'_{α,1}} ... u'_{i'_{α,n_α}} = 1.

This page. For one such relation, the lifts ũ'_{i'_1}, ..., ũ'_{i'_n} in T~ need not be composable. Diagram (9) writes them as a chain of separate arrows s~_{i'_k} -> t~_{i'_k}, with gaps between t~_{i'_k} and s~_{i'_{k-1}}. Both ends of each gap lie over the same object of T.

Grothendieck then supposes a family (a_j)_{j in J} of 'fibre arrows' of T~. On the next page these are required to generate each fibre groupoid T~_s, for every s in Ob T.

Next page. Assume that for each gap, its two endpoints lie in the same connected component of the fibre. Then each gap can be closed by a word M_{α,k}((a_j)) in the fibre generators. The relation M_α then lifts to a closed composite in T~: ũ'_{i_n}, fibre word, ũ'_{i_{n-1}}, ..., fibre word, ũ'_{i_1}.

Where this is going. This is the groupoid version of the classical presentation of a group extension (P. Hall's lemma; the Reidemeister-Schreier / extension method). The expected presentation of T~ has:
- generators ũ_i and a_j;
- relations of three kinds: the fibre relations, the lifted base relations equal to some fibre element, and the conjugation (action) of the ũ_i on the fibre generators.

In the context of cote 146 it serves to present the Teichmüller groupoids T_{g,ν} inductively. One uses the forgetful/fibration maps between levels of the tower (Birman-type exact sequences), building presentations from those of lower complexity. This is the strategy of the Esquisse's claim that the tower is generated by levels 1-2 with relations from levels ≤ 3.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The setup is incomplete: the actual presentation of T~ (including the conjugation/action relations and the fibre relations) is stated only on following pages.

Implicit hypothesis: for the lifted words to close up, p should be a fibration-like (or at least surjective-on-components) functor. The required condition — the gap endpoints lie in one connected component of the fibre — is only stated on the next page as an extra assumption.

ideas.what: Presentation of a groupoid by generators and relations, using signed indices I x {±1} and relations given as words that form loops (lacets)
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid presentation (free groupoid on a graph modulo relators)

ideas.what: Lifting relations of the base groupoid to the total groupoid by closing the gaps between non-composable lifts with paths in the fibres, so as to get a presentation of T~ from presentations of T and of the fibres
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of an extension / fibration of groupoids (groupoid version of P. Hall's extension presentation lemma)
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Hall (groups); groupoid versions folklore, e.g. R. Brown; used for mapping class groups via Birman exact sequence (Birman, Gervais, Wajnryb) and for Teichmüller/Lego groupoids (Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps, Bakalov-Kirillov)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme states the generation/relations principle for the Teichmüller tower without this lemma

missed.claim: Grothendieck formalizes a general groupoid-extension presentation lemma (base presentation + fibre generators + lifted relations closed by fibre paths) as the technical engine for presenting the Teichmüller tower inductively. Later work (HLS 2000, Bakalov-Kirillov) proved such presentations by different, geometric means (cut systems, Hatcher-Thurston complexes).
missed.quote: considérons les flèches ũ'_{i'_1} ⋯ ũ'_{i'_n} de T̃, qui ne sont pas nécessairement composables
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the intended algebraic route to the 'two-level generation, three-level relations' principle of the Esquisse. Of historical interest only; the lemma itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard generalization of the extension-presentation lemma to groupoids. Its interest is mainly historical, as part of Grothendieck's planned proof of presentations for the Teichmüller tower.
transcription_corrections: 'Fl τ' and 'τ̃' should read Fl 𝒯 and 𝒯̃ (same calligraphic T as on the previous page).
(7) is better read as i'_α ∈ I'^{n_α} (the superscript '(α)' is likely a smudged/struck index).
The equation numbering is inconsistent: the previous page's (8) for Î' should be (6), consistent with (7), (8) here.
'flèches-fibre' ('fibre arrows', i.e. arrows of T~ lying in fibres T~_s) seems the right reading of '"flèches"-fibre'.
The last subscript is i'_{α,n_α}, not i'_α, n_α.
